question: Why does Beacon sign people out after 30 minutes, even when they’re still typing?

askedOn.title: PLAT-2234 Signed out of Beacon while typing

answer: Typing in the editor counts as activity only when the `beacon.session.activity-heartbeat` flag is on, so with it off, someone who types without clicking or scrolling is signed out when the site’s idle timeout runs out. That’s 30 minutes unless a site admin has set another value, with a warning 2 minutes before, and clicks, scrolling and page changes always count as activity.

answer.text: The help article {0} still says 60 minutes, which changed to 30 in version 3.0.0. What the identity service does once Beacon asks it to end the session is outside the code we can see.

It takes the length of the timer from the site’s security settings, where a site admin can set an idle timeout (`getSiteIdleTimeout`).

steps.text: Typing in the editor restarts the timer only when the `beacon.session.activity-heartbeat` flag is on. When it’s on, key presses restart it at most once every 30 seconds. When it’s off, typing doesn’t count as activity, so someone can type for the whole timeout and still be signed out (`trackEditorInput`).

reply: Thanks for the details. Beacon signs people out after a period with no activity, and by default that period is 30 minutes. Clicking, scrolling and moving between pages count as activity, so if you’re writing something long, clicking in the page now and then keeps you signed in. Two minutes before you’re signed out, Beacon shows a message with a Stay signed in button. Your site admin can also change how long the period is in the site’s security settings.
